title: Render a Claude Code-imported home session as a Codex 0.156.0 rollout with a kept, changed and lost account
purpose: The home's first cross-harness translation, one named pair and one session: a home session imported from Claude Code is rendered as a Codex rollout that Codex 0.156.0 resumes, in the shape that version writes for its own threads, with every text part, tool call and tool result carried whole, readable thinking carried as text, the thread announcing in band that it is a translation, and an account beside it naming what was kept, what changed shape and what was lost. Codex's own importer of Claude Code files is the recorded baseline: a compaction, not a copy. This brief improves on it and does not adopt it. Nothing above this translation assumes it until its proof holds.
task: Measure first (R1): record what Codex 0.156.0 writes and what it needs to resume, under scratch Codex homes, and take every shape from that recording, never from a source checkout. Then build the Codex profile in crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex (R2 to R6), the codex-render subcommand (R7), the comparison against the recorded rollout (R8), the account written down in RECORD.md (R9) and the resume proof (R10). In scope: one direction (Claude Code-imported home session to Codex), one version (0.156.0), one session per render. Out of scope: Codex to Claude Code; adopting or calling Codex's importer; Pi or any third harness; launching Codex through the launch template; making the Claude Code render deterministic (its random ids for multi-result tool records are a separate defect carded on its own, and this brief's fixture holds none so the hash it stands on is stable). The render writes the rollout under the target's sessions tree and writes no SQLite file: lys-home writes no other harness's database and takes no C SQLite. If R1 measures that 0.156.0 does not replay a rollout that has no state_5.sqlite and thread_history_1.sqlite rows, the index rows are a step of the proof and not of the crate: R1 records the measured answer and the exact sqlite3 statements, and R10 applies them to the scratch home before the resume. Whether Codex can be made to index a rollout it is handed is a later card's question. R1 has two stopping outcomes, each recorded by name in PROOF-CODEX.md and each returning the card to its lead with no crate file changed: 0.156.0 refusing to run without an auth.json, and 0.156.0 writing no function_call for a tool call. Sidechains are carried as spawned threads when R1 measured the 0.156.0 spawned-thread shape; otherwise each is named lost with that reason and carrying them is its own card.

requirements.title: Record the second party: what Codex 0.156.0 writes and what it needs to resume
requirements.spec: Before any file under crates/lys-home/src changes, the builder measures Codex 0.156.0. Every Codex run in this brief uses the Codex binary that answers `codex-cli 0.156.0` to `--version`, with CODEX_HOME set to an empty scratch directory and its working directory an empty scratch directory, and with the API key supplied as the environment variable 0.156.0 reads for an API key, its value read at launch from the operator's existing key file by path, never printed and never written into any file; no auth.json is copied. IF 0.156.0 refuses to run without an auth.json, THEN the builder records under 'Measured before rendering' in PROOF-CODEX.md the line `run: refused without auth.json`, Codex's exit code and the first line Codex printed, creates no file named by R2 to R9, and the brief stops at R1 with the card returned to its lead. Otherwise, in the first scratch home, 0.156.0 writes one thread holding at least two user turns, two assistant replies and one tool call written as a `function_call` with its `function_call_output`, and is asked to spawn one sub-agent thread. The builder copies that thread's rollout, as Codex wrote it, into the fixture directory as `recorded.jsonl`, and a spawned child rollout, when 0.156.0 wrote one, as `recorded-child.jsonl`. IF `recorded.jsonl` holds no `function_call`, THEN the builder records the line `tool call item: no function_call` with the count of each payload type the file holds, creates no file named by R2 to R9, and the brief stops at R1 with the card returned to its lead. The compared set of a rollout is every response_item whose payload is a `message` with role user or assistant, a `function_call` or a `function_call_output`, in file order, excluding a user message whose first `input_text` begins `<environment_context>`. The builder writes `source.claude-code.jsonl`, a Claude Code 2.1.281 file with one record per item of `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set, in order: a user message as a user record with the same texts, an assistant message as an assistant record with the same texts, a `function_call` as an assistant record holding one tool_use with the same name, the call_id as its id and the parsed arguments as its input, and a `function_call_output` as a user record holding one tool_result with the same output. Every record's uuid, and every parentUuid that is not null, is 36 characters with a hyphen at positions 8, 13, 18 and 23 and lowercase hex elsewhere. The builder then records the Claude Code render this brief must leave unchanged, made by the lys-home of the commit the branch is based on, in an empty scratch directory `<scratch>`: `lys-home import --home <scratch>/home --claude-code source.claude-code.jsonl --session fixture`, then `lys-home render --home <scratch>/home --session fixture --uuid 7d3c1a52-9b0e-4f6a-8c21-3e5f0a9b1c44 --cwd /fixture/project --model claude-opus-5-5 --version 2.1.281 --out <scratch>/render/7d3c1a52-9b0e-4f6a-8c21-3e5f0a9b1c44.jsonl`. `claude-code-render.inputs.json` holds those values under the keys `session`, `uuid`, `cwd`, `model`, `version` and `base_commit`; `claude-code-render.sha256` holds the SHA-256 of the rendered JSONL file alone, not of its loss account. Next the builder measures, in a second scratch home holding only `recorded.jsonl` at the path under sessions/ that Codex gave it and no `.sqlite` file, whether `codex resume <thread id>` finds and replays it. IF that resume is refused, THEN the builder reads the rows 0.156.0 wrote for the recorded thread in the first scratch home's state_5.sqlite and thread_history_1.sqlite (and thread_spawn_edges when a child was spawned), writes the matching rows into the second scratch home with the sqlite3 tool, outside lys-home, and measures the resume again. In those statements every value that is transcript text is an expression reading it by path from `recorded.jsonl` with sqlite3's readfile and json_extract, never a literal. PROOF-CODEX.md's 'Measured before rendering' section records: the base commit; each record type and payload type of `recorded.jsonl` with its count; the size of its compared set; `recorded-child.jsonl` as `present` or `absent`; the file-name offset, which is the time in the rollout's file name minus its session_meta payload timestamp truncated to the second, written `+hh:mm` or `-hh:mm`; the index-free resume result as `replayed` or `refused`; and, when refused, the exact statements as text, each table and column they write, and the second result as `replayed` or `refused`. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write a SQLite file from lys-home, SHALL NOT write, copy or read anything under the operator's live Codex home, SHALL NOT take any shape from any source checkout of Codex, SHALL NOT put a user record holding more than one tool_result into `source.claude-code.jsonl`, and the fixtures and PROOF-CODEX.md SHALL NOT hold a credential or any compared-set text.
acceptance: `recorded.jsonl` exists in the fixture directory, its session_meta payload has cli_version equal to "0.156.0", and it holds at least 1 response_item of payload type `function_call` and 1 of payload type `function_call_output` with the same call_id.
`grep -c 'sk-'` over each file in the fixture directory and over PROOF-CODEX.md prints 0, and the fixture directory holds no file named auth.json.

Every uuid and every non-null parentUuid in `source.claude-code.jsonl` matches `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`, and after `lys-home import` of it no entry id in the session `fixture` matches `-r[0-9]+$`.
The number of user and assistant records in `source.claude-code.jsonl` equals the compared-set size PROOF-CODEX.md records, and that size is at least 6.

`claude-code-render.sha256` holds one 64-character lowercase hex string; `claude-code-render.inputs.json` holds session `fixture`, uuid `7d3c1a52-9b0e-4f6a-8c21-3e5f0a9b1c44`, cwd `/fixture/project`, model `claude-opus-5-5`, version `2.1.281` and a 40-character base_commit equal to the base commit PROOF-CODEX.md names.

PROOF-CODEX.md's 'Measured before rendering' section holds the index-free resume result as the word `replayed` or the word `refused`, `recorded-child.jsonl` as the word `present` or the word `absent` matching the fixture directory, and a file-name offset matching `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$`.

WHEN the index-free resume is recorded as `refused`, the section holds at least one sqlite3 INSERT statement naming the table `threads` and a second resume result, and no compared-set text of `recorded.jsonl` 8 or more characters long occurs anywhere in PROOF-CODEX.md.
WHEN PROOF-CODEX.md records `run: refused without auth.json` or `tool call item: no function_call`, `git diff` of the base commit against the branch lists no path under crates/lys-home/src.

requirements.title: The Codex 0.156.0 profile: the measured shape, marker texts, derived ids and the rollout's place
requirements.spec: Create the Codex profile module. harness/codex/mod.rs carries module docs naming the Codex version measured (0.156.0), the fixture it was measured from and the rule that a shape is valid for that version only, `pub mod` declarations, and a `#[cfg(test)]` `mod <name>_tests;` declaration for each sibling test file, as harness/claude_code/mod.rs does, and nothing else. shape-0.156.0.json holds the values measured from `recorded.jsonl` and `recorded-child.jsonl` that are not transcript text, not ids and not timestamps: `session_meta`, the recorded session_meta payload without id, session_id, timestamp and context_window.window_id, base_instructions kept as recorded because it is the instruction text Codex wrote for its own thread and not transcript text; `turn_context`, the first recorded turn_context payload without turn_id, root_turn_id and current_date; `task_started`, its model_context_window and collaboration_mode_kind; `items`, for each payload type and role of the compared set, the keys the recorded payload carries, the prefix of its `id`, and the recorded constant values of `phase` for an assistant message that ends its turn and for one that does not (null where the recording holds no such message) and of the metadata passthrough's `content_item_kinds`; `file_name_offset`, as R1 recorded it; and `spawned_child`, null when `recorded-child.jsonl` is absent, otherwise an object holding the child's session_meta payload without its ids and timestamps and `parent_link`, the JSON pointers into that payload whose recorded value equals the parent's thread id. In `session_meta`, `turn_context` and `spawned_child`, every string equal to the recorded working directory, or beginning with it followed by `/`, holds `{cwd}` in place of that directory. profile.rs loads the embedded shape into a `Shape` value, which every render function takes as a parameter; holds the one supported version string "0.156.0", the mapping name "codex-0.156.0 render v1" and the three marker texts (translation: `[lys translated context] This thread is a translation, not the original session. Source session: <session id>. Rendered by lys-home <crate version> (<git commit>) with mapping codex-0.156.0 render v1.`; authored: `[lys authored turn] A person wrote this reply; no model produced it.`; inherited: `[lys inherited] Carried from session <from_session>: a predecessor's memory, not this session's own experience.`); and defines the derived id: a UUID version 7 whose 48-bit time field is a given RFC 3339 timestamp's Unix milliseconds, whose version and variant bits are set as RFC 9562 names them, and whose other 74 bits are the leading 74 bits of SHA-256 over the given seed strings, each followed by one NUL byte. The thread id is the derived id of the home session header's timestamp over the seeds (session id, id of the last entry on the context path); the context window id is the derived id of the header timestamp over (session id, `context_window`). The rollout path is `<target>/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-YYYY-MM-DDThh-mm-ss-<thread id>.jsonl`, every field taken from the header timestamp shifted by the shape's `file_name_offset`; the account path is the rollout path with `.jsonl` replaced by `.loss.json`. build.rs records the git commit the crate is built from as a compile-time value; IF no commit can be read, THEN the build SHALL fail naming why. WHEN a version other than "0.156.0" is asked for, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it by name. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT mint a random id, SHALL NOT read the clock or the process's time zone for any value in the rollout, and SHALL NOT take a shape value from anywhere but the recorded fixtures.
acceptance: For session id `s`, header timestamp `2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` and last context entry id `e9`, the thread id is the same string on two calls, parses as a UUID whose version is 7 and whose variant is RFC 9562's, and its first 12 hex digits with hyphens removed are `00dc6acfac00`, the timestamp's Unix milliseconds as 12 lowercase hex digits.

With target `/t`, header timestamp `2000-01-01T15:30:00.000Z` and file_name_offset `+10:00`, the rollout path is `/t/sessions/2000/01/02/rollout-2000-01-02T01-30-00-<thread id>.jsonl` and the account path is the same path ending `.loss.json` in place of `.jsonl`.
Asking the profile for version `0.155.0` returns an error whose message contains `0.155.0` and `0.156.0`.
Every non-blank, non-comment line of harness/codex/mod.rs is a `pub mod <name>;` line, a `pub use` line, a `#[cfg(test)]` line or a `mod <name>_tests;` line.

For every key of the shape's `session_meta`, replacing `{cwd}` with `recorded.jsonl`'s session_meta cwd gives that key's value in `recorded.jsonl`'s session_meta payload; the same holds for `turn_context` against `recorded.jsonl`'s first turn_context payload.
The shape's `file_name_offset` equals the offset PROOF-CODEX.md records, and its `spawned_child` is null exactly when `recorded-child.jsonl` is absent from the fixture directory.

requirements.title: The account: kept, changed and lost, by entry id and block hash
requirements.spec: Define the account written beside a rollout as one JSON object: `source_session` (the home session id), `thread_id`, `mapping` ("codex-0.156.0 render v1"), `rollout` (its path), `child_rollouts` (one object per spawned child rollout, with `thread_id` and `rollout`; empty when there is none), and three arrays of rows. Every row carries `entry_id`, `part` (the part's index in the entry's content, or null for a whole entry), `hash`, `hash_kind` and `blocks`. `kept`: one row per part carried as the Codex item native to its kind with its content unchanged, adding `kind` (the home part kind) and `item` (the Codex item or part kind it became). `changed`: one row per part or entry carried in another kind or with something removed or added, adding `before`, `after` and `how` (a fixed phrase naming the change, never content). `lost`: one row per part or entry not carried, adding `kind` and `reason` (a fixed phrase, never content). Hashes: where the entry names a block hash for the part, `hash` is that block hash and `hash_kind` is `block`, never a second hash of the same bytes; where the part is held inline in the entry with no block named, `hash` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of `serde_json::to_vec` of the part as parsed from the entry and `hash_kind` is `inline`; a whole entry's `hash` is the SHA-256 of `serde_json::to_vec` of the entry, `inline`. `blocks` lists, in the order the entry names them, every block hash the entry names for that part or entry (for a lys.call entry its request parts, response parts, raw request and raw response), and is empty otherwise. The account reads what the entry names and does not change how any entry is imported. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write any transcript text, argument, output or thinking into the account, SHALL NOT give a `block` hash that does not resolve in the home's blocks store, SHALL NOT list one part in two arrays, and SHALL NOT omit a part or entry of the context path from all three.
acceptance: An account built for an entry `e1` with parts [text, thinking with signature, redacted thinking] lists part 0 in `kept` with kind `text` and item `output_text`, part 1 in `changed` with before `thinking` and after `output_text`, and part 2 in `lost` with kind `thinking` and reason `redacted thinking: opaque to another provider`; the three rows together number 3.
The `hash` for part 0 equals the SHA-256 of `serde_json::to_vec` of that part as the entry holds it, and its `hash_kind` is `inline` and its `blocks` is empty.

A lys.call entry naming 2 request parts and a raw response, each put in the home's block store, is listed once in `lost` with `blocks` holding those 3 hashes in that order, and `BlockStore::get` returns the stored bytes for each.
The serialised account for a fixture whose texts each contain the string `CANARY-7f3a` contains 0 occurrences of `CANARY-7f3a`.

requirements.title: Home entries into Codex items, carried whole
requirements.spec: Map each context-path entry to Codex 0.156.0 response items, each payload carrying exactly the keys the shape's `items` records for its payload type and role. `id` is the recorded prefix followed by the derived id of the entry's timestamp over (session id, entry id, part index in decimal); the metadata passthrough carries `turn_id` (the turn R5 places the item in), `create_time` (the entry's timestamp as Unix seconds with its milliseconds as the fraction) and `content_item_kinds` from the shape; an assistant message carries the shape's `phase` for a message that ends its turn when it is the last assistant message of its turn and the other recorded `phase` otherwise, and no `phase` key when that value is null. A user message becomes a `message` with role user and one `input_text` per text part, the text byte-identical. An assistant message becomes, in part order: consecutive text and readable-thinking parts gathered into one `message` with role assistant and one `output_text` per part, and each toolCall part a `function_call` with `name` the tool name, `call_id` the tool call id and `arguments` a JSON text whose parsed value equals the toolCall's arguments value; writing the value as text is the only change, as Codex's own function_call carries arguments. A toolResult message becomes a `function_call_output` with `call_id` the tool call id; WHEN the toolResult holds exactly one part and it is text, `output` is that text as a string, byte-identical; otherwise `output` is a list with one `input_text` per text part, byte-identical, and one `input_image` per image part with `image_url` the data URL `data:<media type>;base64,<data>`, in part order. An image part in a user message becomes an `input_image` in the same way. WHEN a thinking part carries readable text, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry that text as an `output_text` and list it as changed (before `thinking`, after `output_text`, how `signature dropped` when it had one and `carried as text` when it had none); IF a thinking part is redacted or its text is empty, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL drop it and list it as lost by hash with reason `redacted thinking: opaque to another provider` or `empty thinking` respectively. WHEN an assistant message's model is `authored`, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry it as an assistant message whose first `output_text` is the authored marker and list it as changed with how `authored marker added`; an assistant message whose model is not `authored` carries no authored marker. A lys.authored entry produces no item and is listed as changed with how `carried as the authored marker`. WHEN a user or assistant message's entry id is one of the `from_entries` of a lys.inherited entry on the context path that names a `from_session`, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry it in its own role with the inherited marker, naming that `from_session`, as its first text part, and list it as changed with how `inherited marker added`. A lys.inherited entry produces no item and is listed as changed with how `carried as the inherited marker` when it names a `from_session` and `carried as the authored marker` when it does not. WHEN a toolResult has isError true, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry it and list it as changed with how `is_error flag not carried`. A compaction entry becomes a user `message` whose one `input_text` is the summary, listed as changed with how `compaction summary as a user message`. A lys.harness_event, lys.call or any other lys custom entry, a label, and every other entry type are lost with a reason naming the entry type or customType; a part kind with no Codex item is lost with a reason naming the kind. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT drop a lys.authored or lys.inherited entry as lost, SHALL NOT truncate, clip or summarise any text, argument or output, SHALL NOT change the JSON value of any argument, SHALL NOT write a `reasoning` item, and SHALL NOT write any signature or redacted data into an item.
acceptance: A toolResult whose one text part is 10,000 characters becomes a `function_call_output` whose `output` is a string of 10,000 characters with the same SHA-256 as the source text.
A toolCall with arguments `{"timeout":5,"command":"ls -la"}` becomes a `function_call` whose `arguments`, parsed, equals that JSON value and whose `call_id` equals the toolCall id.

An assistant entry [signed thinking `look first`, text `done`] becomes one assistant `message` with two `output_text` parts, `look first` then `done`, and no item in the output contains the signature string.

A context path of 6 assistant messages with model `authored` followed by 1 assistant message with model `claude-opus-5-5` gives 7 assistant messages: each of the first 6 has first `output_text` equal to `[lys authored turn] A person wrote this reply; no model produced it.`, the 7th holds no `output_text` equal to it, and the account lists the first 6 in `changed` and none of them in `lost`.

A toolResult holding one text part and one image part with media type `image/png` becomes a `function_call_output` whose `output` is a list of an `input_text` then an `input_image` whose `image_url` begins `data:image/png;base64,`.
A user message listed in a lys.inherited entry with from_session `s0` stays role user and its first `input_text` equals the inherited marker with `<from_session>` replaced by `s0`.

A lys.harness_event entry, a label entry and a `document` part each appear once in the account's `lost` with a reason naming `lys.harness_event`, `label` and `document` respectively, and produce no item.

requirements.title: Render the context path to a rollout beside its account
requirements.spec: WHEN codex-render is asked for a session and a target directory, THE SYSTEM SHALL walk the session's context path as the Claude Code render does (Session::context_path) and write the rollout at the R2 path. Turns: a turn opens at each context-path entry that renders to a user message (a user message entry or a compaction entry) and at the first rendered entry when that is not one, and closes before the next opening or at the path's end; each turn's id is the derived id of its opening entry's timestamp over (session id, opening entry id). Records, in order: a session_meta record whose payload is the shape's `session_meta` with `{cwd}` replaced by the home session header's cwd, and id and session_id the thread id, timestamp the header timestamp, and context_window.window_id the context window id; then for each turn an event_msg `task_started` (turn_id and root_turn_id the turn id, started_at the opening entry's timestamp in Unix seconds, and the shape's `task_started` values), a turn_context record (the shape's `turn_context` with `{cwd}` replaced, turn_id and root_turn_id the turn id, and current_date the opening entry's date shifted by the shape's `file_name_offset`), in the first turn only a developer `message` whose one `input_text` is the translation marker with the source session id, the crate version and the build commit filled in, the turn's R4 items in path order, and an event_msg `task_complete` (turn_id; started_at; completed_at the turn's last entry's timestamp in Unix seconds; duration_ms that timestamp minus the opening one in milliseconds; time_to_first_token_ms the first assistant entry's timestamp in the turn minus the opening one in milliseconds, 0 when the turn has none; last_agent_message the last `output_text` of the turn's last assistant message, byte-identical, null when the turn has none). Every record carries exactly the top-level keys `timestamp`, `ordinal` (its 0-based line index), `type` and `payload`; `timestamp` is written `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.mmmZ` in UTC and is the header timestamp for session_meta, the opening entry's for task_started, turn_context and the marker, the turn's last entry's for task_complete, and the source entry's for an item. Then THE SYSTEM SHALL write the R3 account at the R2 account path. IF the rollout path or the account path exists, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return HomeError::Exists naming that path and SHALL create no file and no directory. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write under any directory but the target, SHALL NOT write any SQLite file, SHALL NOT write a token_count, token_usage_record, item_completed, realtime_item or world_state record, and SHALL NOT append to, open for writing or rewrite any file of the home.
acceptance: Rendering the same session twice to one target: the second call returns HomeError::Exists whose path equals the first call's rollout path, and a listing of every file under the target with its size and SHA-256 is identical before and after the second call.
With only the account path pre-created as an empty file, the call returns HomeError::Exists naming the account path and no rollout file exists afterwards.

For a path [user, assistant, user, assistant] the rollout's record types in order are session_meta, event_msg task_started, turn_context, response_item developer message, user message, assistant message, event_msg task_complete, event_msg task_started, turn_context, user message, assistant message, event_msg task_complete, and each record's `ordinal` equals its line index.
The developer message's text contains the source session id and `codex-0.156.0 render v1`, and the session_meta payload's id equals the thread id in the rollout's file name.
Two renders of one session to two empty targets produce rollouts with the same SHA-256.
The home session file, its index and its head file have the same SHA-256 before and after a render, and the home's blocks directory holds the same file count.
No file whose name ends `.sqlite` exists under the target after a render.

requirements.title: Sidechains as spawned threads, in the measured shape
requirements.spec: A sidechain is the entry a label entry names by `targetId` when its label begins `agent `, together with every entry descending from it; sidechain.rs finds them by reading the home session file line by line, read-only, and keeps file order. WHILE the shape's `spawned_child` is not null, THE SYSTEM SHALL render each sidechain as its own child rollout under the target: its thread id is the derived id of the sidechain's first entry's timestamp over (session id, first sidechain entry id); its path follows the R2 rule from that timestamp and thread id; its session_meta payload is `spawned_child`'s payload with `{cwd}` replaced, id and session_id the child's thread id, and the parent's thread id written at each of `parent_link`'s pointers; its turns and items follow R5 and R4 over the sidechain's entries, without the translation marker. The account lists each sidechain part as kept, changed or lost as R4 rules, lists the label entry as changed with how `carried as a spawned thread's parent link`, and names each child in `child_rollouts`. IF `spawned_child` is null, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL write no child rollout and list each sidechain entry and its label in `lost` with reason `sidechain: 0.156.0 spawned-thread shape not measured here`. codex/render.rs calls this step after the parent's items, and checks every child rollout path for existence, refusing as R5 does, before it writes any file. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write a thread_spawn_edges row or any SQLite file, and SHALL NOT place a sidechain's items in the parent rollout.
acceptance: With a Shape whose `spawned_child` is `{"session_meta": {"parent": ""}, "parent_link": ["/parent"]}`, a fixture session with one sidechain of 2 message entries renders to 2 rollout files under the target, the child's session_meta payload at `/parent` equals the parent rollout's thread id, and the account's `child_rollouts` holds 1 object whose `rollout` is the child's path.

With the same fixture and a Shape whose `spawned_child` is null, the render writes 1 rollout file and the account's `lost` holds 3 rows, the 2 sidechain entries and their label, each with reason `sidechain: 0.156.0 spawned-thread shape not measured here`.
In both cases the parent rollout holds 0 items whose `id` is derived from a sidechain entry id.
With the child rollout path pre-created, the render returns HomeError::Exists naming that path and the parent rollout does not exist afterwards.

requirements.title: The codex-render subcommand and its report
requirements.spec: Add the `codex-render` subcommand with `--home`, `--session`, `--target` (the directory the rollout is written under, which the proof uses as the Codex home) and `--codex-version`, all required. Its argument struct and run function live in harness/codex/command.rs; cli.rs gains only the enum variant and one dispatch arm. WHEN it succeeds, THE SYSTEM SHALL print one JSON object: `command` (`codex-render`), `rollout` (path), `account` (path), `entries` (context-path entries walked), `blocks` (parts walked), `kept`, `changed` and `lost` (the account's array lengths), and `child_rollouts` (paths). THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT print, log or put in an error any transcript text, argument, output, thinking or marker text, and SHALL NOT launch Codex or any other program.
